title: SharePoint: edit, version, restore and copy site skills in Copilot in SharePoint
summary: The documented management actions, licensing and control calls are supported, but the default is incorrectly reported as unstated. Microsoft documents skills as an available capability that users choose to create and use, without a separate administrative activation step. The checklist also names permission and audit controls missing from the controls table.

Restricted Content Discovery is set in SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing site-level control that removes Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions from a restricted site.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing setting that's respected. If it's enabled on a site, Copilot in SharePoint and AI actions don't appear on that site. This rule applies regardless of your other availability settings.

claims.claim: Site owners reach the site-skill management page through Settings > Site skills.
claims.quote: To manage the skills associated with a site, select Settings > Site skills. To review or restore an earlier version, open the skill and select the Versions tab.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct list but stops before individual controls. Keep 'Settings > Site skills' and add to its note: 'For version restore, select the skill name or Open, then Versions.' claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the default availability of the site-skill management capability.
claims.quote: There are no separate admin controls to turn skills on or off. By default, any user with Edit permissions on the site can create a site skill, and any user with View permissions can use it.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'user-opt-in'. Replace 'Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival, so base your plan on no source saying that existing behaviour changes' with 'Site skills are available within Copilot in SharePoint without a separate skills admin switch; users choose to create or use them, subject to site permissions.' In Open questions, remove 'Will Microsoft state a default for these management features, or' and retain the question about a future tenant-level switch. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/copilot-in-sharepoint-skills and https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/copilot-in-sharepoint-get-started.
